title: Revision: the advanced tracks
problem: You have read seven advanced modules, and the next interviewer will name a problem, not a lesson.
summary: Flashcards for modules 7 to 13: each card names a problem from the distributed, database, streaming, reliability, security, infrastructure and architecture tracks. Answer with the building block, flip to check, and use the table to find the lesson to reread.
catTip: I revise the way I hunt: the problem appears, and the answer must already be in my paws. If I have to think about it, the mouse has left. Flip the card, then say the next one faster.

recall.q: Problem: "two nodes both believe they are the leader." Which building block, and what stops the old leader doing damage?
recall.a: Leader election with fencing: each new leader gets a higher token, and the storage layer rejects writes carrying an older one, so a stale leader cannot corrupt anything even if it keeps running.

guide.breaks: Without recall practice you recognise every advanced block on the page and still freeze when an interviewer describes the problem and waits, because reading built recognition, not retrieval.
guide.tradeoffs: Flashcards are slower and less comfortable than rereading, and the cards you miss keep returning until you know them; that discomfort is the mechanism.
guide.explainSimply: This page is a deck of cards. Each one describes something going wrong in a big system, and you say which tool fixes it before turning the card over. The table below the deck shows every answer with the lesson it came from.
guide.hint: Think about what a new leader needs that an old one cannot forge.

meow: Problem in, block out, faster each lap. Seven tracks, one deck, whiskers up if you knew it.
